passages.text: Oh, that my head were a spring of water, and my eyes a fountain of tears! I would weep day and night over the slain daughter of my people.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks.
He feels deep sorrow for his people.
He wishes his head were a spring of water.
He wishes his eyes were a fountain of tears.
He wants to weep day and night.
He mourns for the people who have died.
He calls them the slain daughter of his people.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִתֵּ֤ן רֹאשִׁי֙ מַ֔יִם וְעֵינִ֖י מְק֣וֹר דִּמְעָ֑ה וְאֶבְכֶּה֙ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלַ֔יְלָה אֵ֖ת חַֽלְלֵ֥י בַת־ עַמִּֽי׃

passages.text: If only I had a traveler’s lodge in the wilderness, I would abandon my people and depart from them, for they are all adulterers, a crowd of faithless people.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Jeremiah speaks for God’s people.
Jeremiah feels deep sorrow for his people’s sins.
He wishes for a place to escape.
He wants a traveler’s lodge in the wilderness.
He wants to leave his people and go far away.
He wants to separate himself from them.
All his people commit adultery.
They are unfaithful to God.
They are a crowd of traitors.
They betray trust and break faith.
passages.original: מִֽי־ יִתְּנֵ֣נִי בַמִּדְבָּ֗ר מְלוֹן֙ אֹֽרְחִ֔ים וְאֶֽעֶזְבָה֙ אֶת־ עַמִּ֔י וְאֵלְכָ֖ה מֵֽאִתָּ֑ם כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים׃

passages.text: “They bend their tongues like bows; lies prevail over truth in the land. For they proceed from evil to evil, and they do not take Me into account,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The people act with evil hearts.
They use their tongues like bows.
They shoot out lies.
Lies become strong in the land.
Truth does not rule.
The people move from one evil to another evil.
They do not know the LORD.
They do not think about the LORD.
passages.original: וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ אֶת־ לְשׁוֹנָם֙ קַשְׁתָּ֣ם שֶׁ֔קֶר וְלֹ֥א לֶאֱמוּנָ֖ה גָּבְר֣וּ בָאָ֑רֶץ כִּי֩ מֵרָעָ֨ה אֶל־ רָעָ֧ה׀ יָצָ֛אוּ וְאֹתִ֥י לֹֽא־ יָדָ֖עוּ נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Let everyone guard against his neighbor; do not trust any brother, for every brother deals craftily, and every friend spreads slander.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to His people.
He warns them about their relationships.
Each person must guard himself against his neighbor.
Do not trust any brother.
Every brother acts deceitfully.
Every friend spreads slander.
passages.original: אִ֤ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ הִשָּׁמֵ֔רוּ וְעַל־ כָּל־ אָ֖ח אַל־ תִּבְטָ֑חוּ כִּ֤י כָל־ אָח֙ עָק֣וֹב יַעְקֹ֔ב וְכָל־ רֵ֖עַ רָכִ֥יל יַהֲלֹֽךְ׃

passages.text: Each one betrays his friend; no one tells the truth. They have taught their tongues to lie; they wear themselves out committing iniquity.
passages.sermon:
The people in this passage live in a land filled with lies and deceit.
Each person betrays his friend.
No one speaks the truth.
They have trained their tongues to speak lies.
They grow tired from doing evil.
passages.original: וְאִ֤ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ יְהָתֵ֔לּוּ וֶאֱמֶ֖ת לֹ֣א יְדַבֵּ֑רוּ לִמְּד֧וּ לְשׁוֹנָ֛ם דַּבֶּר־ שֶׁ֖קֶר הַעֲוֵ֥ה נִלְאֽוּ׃

passages.text: You dwell in the midst of deception; in their deceit they refuse to know Me,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says this to the people of Judah.
You live among people who deceive.
Deception surrounds you.
These people choose to deceive.
They refuse to know Me.
They do this because of their deceit.
This is what the LORD declares.
passages.original: שִׁבְתְּךָ֖ בְּת֣וֹךְ מִרְמָ֑ה בְּמִרְמָ֛ה מֵאֲנ֥וּ דַֽעַת־ אוֹתִ֖י נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Behold, I will refine them and test them, for what else can I do because of the daughter of My people?
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He says, “I will refine My people.
I will test them.
I must do this because of the sins of My people.
I have no other choice.
My people have become corrupt.
They are like silver that needs to be purified.
I must act for the sake of My people.”
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י צוֹרְפָ֖ם וּבְחַנְתִּ֑ים כִּֽי־ אֵ֣יךְ אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה מִפְּנֵ֖י בַּת־ עַמִּֽי׃

passages.text: Their tongues are deadly arrows; they speak deception. With his mouth a man speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he sets a trap for him.
passages.sermon:
The people speak with tongues that are like deadly arrows.
They use their words to deceive others.
A man says peaceful things to his neighbor with his mouth.
But in his heart, he plans to trap his neighbor.
passages.original: חֵ֥ץ שׁוֹחֵט לְשׁוֹנָ֖ם מִרְמָ֣ה דִבֵּ֑ר בְּפִ֗יו שָׁל֤וֹם אֶת־ רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ יְדַבֵּ֔ר וּבְקִרְבּ֖וֹ יָשִׂ֥ים אָרְבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Should I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this?”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
The LORD sees the sins of the people.
The LORD asks a question.
Should I not punish these people for their actions?
The LORD declares His right to judge.
Should I not take vengeance on a nation like this?
The LORD demands justice for their wrongdoing.
passages.original: הַעַל־ אֵ֥לֶּה לֹֽא־ אֶפְקָד־ בָּ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה אִ֚ם בְּג֣וֹי אֲשֶׁר־ כָּזֶ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתְנַקֵּ֖ם נַפְשִֽׁי׃ס

passages.text: I will take up a weeping and wailing for the mountains, a dirge over the wilderness pasture, for they have been scorched so no one passes through, and the lowing of cattle is not heard. Both the birds of the air and the beasts have fled; they have gone away.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, “I will weep for the mountains.
I will wail for the mountains.
I will sing a dirge for the pastures in the wilderness.
The pastures are scorched.
No one passes through them.
No one hears the sound of cattle there.
The birds of the sky have fled.
The animals have also gone away.
The land is empty and deserted.”
passages.original: עַל־ הֶ֨הָרִ֜ים אֶשָּׂ֧א בְכִ֣י וָנֶ֗הִי וְעַל־ נְא֤וֹת מִדְבָּר֙ קִינָ֔ה כִּ֤י נִצְּתוּ֙ מִבְּלִי־ אִ֣ישׁ עֹבֵ֔ר וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֖וּ ק֣וֹל מִקְנֶ֑ה מֵע֤וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְעַד־ בְּהֵמָ֔ה נָדְד֖וּ הָלָֽכוּ׃

passages.text: “And I will make Jerusalem a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD will punish Jerusalem.
The LORD will make Jerusalem a heap of rubble.
Jackals will live among the ruins of Jerusalem.
The LORD will destroy the cities of Judah.
No one will live in the cities of Judah.
The cities of Judah will become empty and desolate.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לְגַלִּ֖ים מְע֣וֹן תַּנִּ֑ים וְאֶת־ עָרֵ֧י יְהוּדָ֛ה אֶתֵּ֥ן שְׁמָמָ֖ה מִבְּלִ֖י יוֹשֵֽׁב׃ס

passages.text: Who is the man wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that he may explain it? Why is the land destroyed and scorched like a desert, so no one can pass through it?
passages.sermon:
A wise man can understand this.
The LORD must speak to him.
He can explain the meaning.
The land is destroyed.
The land is scorched like a desert.
No one can pass through the land.
passages.original: מִֽי־ הָאִ֤ישׁ הֶֽחָכָם֙ וְיָבֵ֣ן אֶת־ זֹ֔את וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר פִּֽי־ יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו וְיַגִּדָ֑הּ עַל־ מָה֙ אָבְדָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ נִצְּתָ֥ה כַמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִבְּלִ֖י עֹבֵֽר׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD answered, “It is because they have forsaken My law, which I set before them; they have not walked in it or obeyed My voice.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke.
The LORD explained the reason for the destruction.
The people abandoned the LORD’s law.
The LORD gave this law to them.
The people did not listen to the LORD’s voice.
The people did not walk in the LORD’s law.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֔ה עַל־ עָזְבָם֙ אֶת־ תּ֣וֹרָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִפְנֵיהֶ֑ם וְלֹא־ שָׁמְע֥וּ בְקוֹלִ֖י וְלֹא־ הָ֥לְכוּ בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Instead, they have followed the stubbornness of their hearts and gone after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.”
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel acted stubbornly.
They followed the desires of their own hearts.
They did not obey God.
They went after the Baals.
Their fathers taught them to do this.
They learned these ways from their ancestors.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לְכ֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י שְׁרִר֣וּת לִבָּ֑ם וְאַחֲרֵי֙ הַבְּעָלִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לִמְּד֖וּם אֲבוֹתָֽם׃ס

passages.text: Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I will feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He says these words.
I will act because of what the people have done.
I will feed this people bitter food.
I will give them wormwood to eat.
I will give them poisoned water to drink.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה־ אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הִנְנִ֧י מַאֲכִילָ֛ם אֶת־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה לַֽעֲנָ֑ה וְהִשְׁקִיתִ֖ים מֵי־ רֹֽאשׁ׃

passages.text: I will scatter them among the nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send a sword after them until I have finished them off.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD speaks to His people.
The LORD says, “I will scatter this people among the nations.
These nations are unknown to them.
Their fathers did not know these nations either.
I will send a sword after them.
The sword will pursue them until I have finished them.”
passages.original: וַהֲפִֽצוֹתִים֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יָֽדְע֔וּ הֵ֖מָּה וַֽאֲבוֹתָ֑ם וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַֽחֲרֵיהֶם֙ אֶת־ הַחֶ֔רֶב עַ֥ד כַּלּוֹתִ֖י אוֹתָֽם׃פ

passages.text: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Take note, and summon the wailing women; send for the most skillful among them.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He gives a command.
He says, "Pay attention."
He says, "Call for the wailing women."
He says, "Let the wailing women come."
He says, "Send for the most skillful women."
He says, "Let the skillful women come."
passages.original: כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִתְבּֽוֹנְנ֛וּ וְקִרְא֥וּ לַמְקוֹנְנ֖וֹת וּתְבוֹאֶ֑ינָה וְאֶל־ הַחֲכָמ֥וֹת שִׁלְח֖וּ וְתָבֽוֹאנָה׃

passages.text: Let them come quickly and take up a lament over us, that our eyes may overflow with tears, and our eyelids may gush with water.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
He commands the people to call the wailing women.
Let the wailing women come quickly.
Let them begin to mourn over us.
Our eyes will fill with tears.
Our eyelids will pour out water.
passages.original: וּתְמַהֵ֕רְנָה וְתִשֶּׂ֥נָה עָלֵ֖ינוּ נֶ֑הִי וְתֵרַ֤דְנָה עֵינֵ֙ינוּ֙ דִּמְעָ֔ה וְעַפְעַפֵּ֖ינוּ יִזְּלוּ־ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: For the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: ‘How devastated we are! How great is our shame! For we have abandoned the land because our dwellings have been torn down.’ ”
passages.sermon:
The people of Zion cry out with loud wailing.
They say, “We are devastated.
We feel deep shame.
We have left our land.
Our homes have been destroyed.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י ק֥וֹל נְהִ֛י נִשְׁמַ֥ע מִצִּיּ֖וֹן אֵ֣יךְ שֻׁדָּ֑דְנוּ בֹּ֤שְׁנֽוּ מְאֹד֙ כִּֽי־ עָזַ֣בְנוּ אָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י הִשְׁלִ֖יכוּ מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֵֽינוּ׃ס

passages.text: Now, O women, hear the word of the LORD. Open your ears to the word of His mouth. Teach your daughters to wail, and one another to lament.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the women of Israel.
Women, listen to the word of the LORD.
Pay attention to what He says.
Teach your daughters to wail.
Teach each woman to sing a song of mourning to her friend.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ שְׁמַ֤עְנָה נָשִׁים֙ דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֔ה וְתִקַּ֥ח אָזְנְכֶ֖ם דְּבַר־ פִּ֑יו וְלַמֵּ֤דְנָה בְנֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ נֶ֔הִי וְאִשָּׁ֥ה רְעוּתָ֖הּ קִינָֽה׃

passages.text: For death has climbed in through our windows; it has entered our fortresses to cut off the children from the streets, the young men from the town squares.
passages.sermon:
Death has come into our homes.
Death has entered through our windows.
Death has invaded our strong buildings.
Death has come to destroy our children outside.
Death has come to remove the young men from the public squares.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ עָ֤לָה מָ֙וֶת֙ בְּחַלּוֹנֵ֔ינוּ בָּ֖א בְּאַרְמְנוֹתֵ֑ינוּ לְהַכְרִ֤ית עוֹלָל֙ מִח֔וּץ בַּחוּרִ֖ים מֵרְחֹבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Declare that this is what the LORD says: “The corpses of men will fall like dung upon the open field, like newly cut grain behind the reaper, with no one to gather it.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks with authority.
He commands you to declare His words.
The LORD says this.
The dead bodies of men will fall.
They will lie on the open field.
They will be like dung on the ground.
They will be like stalks of grain left behind after the reaper cuts them.
No one will gather these bodies.
No one will collect them.
passages.original: דַּבֵּ֗ר כֹּ֚ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה וְנָֽפְלָה֙ נִבְלַ֣ת הָֽאָדָ֔ם כְּדֹ֖מֶן עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּכְעָמִ֛יר מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י הַקֹּצֵ֖ר וְאֵ֥ין מְאַסֵּֽף׃ס

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the wealthy man in his riches.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD gives a command.
Do not let the wise man boast about his wisdom.
Do not let the strong man boast about his strength.
Do not let the rich man boast about his riches.
passages.original: כֹּ֣ה׀ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל־ יִתְהַלֵּ֤ל חָכָם֙ בְּחָכְמָת֔וֹ וְאַל־ יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל הַגִּבּ֖וֹר בִּגְבֽוּרָת֑וֹ אַל־ יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל עָשִׁ֖יר בְּעָשְׁרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: But let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD, who exercises loving devotion, justice and righteousness on the earth— for I delight in these things,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD has loving devotion.
The LORD does justice.
The LORD does righteousness on the earth.
The LORD delights in loving devotion, justice, and righteousness.
If anyone boasts, let him boast in this.
Let him boast that he understands and knows the LORD.
The LORD declares these things.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אִם־ בְּזֹ֞את יִתְהַלֵּ֣ל הַמִּתְהַלֵּ֗ל הַשְׂכֵּל֮ וְיָדֹ֣עַ אוֹתִי֒ כִּ֚י אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֔ה עֹ֥שֶׂה חֶ֛סֶד מִשְׁפָּ֥ט וּצְדָקָ֖ה בָּאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־ בְאֵ֥לֶּה חָפַ֖צְתִּי נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: “Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will punish all who are circumcised yet uncircumcised: Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and all the inhabitants of the desert who clip the hair of their temples. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
He says, “The days are coming.
I will punish all who are circumcised in the flesh but remain uncircumcised in heart.
I will punish Egypt.
I will punish Judah.
I will punish Edom.
I will punish the people of Ammon.
I will punish Moab.
I will punish all who live in the desert and cut the hair at their temples.
All these nations are uncircumcised.
The whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.”
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה וּפָ֣קַדְתִּ֔י עַל־ כָּל־ מ֖וּל בְּעָרְלָֽה׃ עַל־ מִצְרַ֣יִם וְעַל־ יְהוּדָ֗ה וְעַל־ אֱד֞וֹם וְעַל־ בְּנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ וְעַל־ מוֹאָ֔ב וְעַל֙ כָּל־ קְצוּצֵ֣י פֵאָ֔ה הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּ֤י כָל־ הַגּוֹיִם֙ עֲרֵלִ֔ים וְכָל־ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עַרְלֵי־ לֵֽב׃ס
